<thought>Based on the ¹H NMR data: a singlet 3H at 2.23 ppm suggests an acetyl methyl (CH₃‑C=O). Two triplets (2H each) at 2.81 and 2.98 ppm with the same J ≈ 7 Hz indicate a –CH₂‑CH₂‑ fragment, likely CH₂‑CO and CH₂‑Ar. The aromatic region shows 9 protons total (7 H at 7.17 ppm and 2 H at 7.90 ppm), consistent with a phenyl ring (5 H) plus a monosubstituted benzene fused to another aromatic system (e.g., a naphthyl group). Combining these clues points to the structure **acetophenone‑CH₂‑CH₂‑Ph**, i.e., phenethyl phenyl ketone (1‑phenyl‑2‑phenylethanone). Its SMILES is `CC(=O)CCc1ccccc1`. This matches the observed proton pattern: CH₃‑C=O (2.23 s, 3H), α‑CH₂ to carbonyl (2.81 t, 2H), β‑CH₂ next to phenyl (2.98 t, 2H), and the phenyl ring (5 H) plus the additional aromatic protons from the carbonyl‑attached phenyl (4 H) giving the observed 9 aromatic protons. 

Thus the SMILES string is: `CC(=O)CCc1ccccc1`.
